messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] plot_coeff with quadratic covariates
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] plot_coeff with quadratic covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
yes, this is intended. For continuous covariates with a linear and quadratic effect, plot_effects will combine both effects into one response curve. This works because both effects are additive and can use a shared x axis showing the covariate values.

plot_coef on the other hand shows you the effect strength of both parameters separately, with effect strength on the x axis. Since the linear and quadratic effects are independent (basically like the independent covariates) they cannot be combined in plot_coef (or rather, that would result in overlapping data in the plot / overplotting).

Best regards,
Jürgen

Hello Camtrap R Community,

I have a question related to formatting time differences for using the timeshift function.

When working with time differences in the "years:months:days hours:minutes:seconds" format, I encountered a scenario where the difference is 40 days. I would like to clarify the appropriate way to express this duration in the specified format. Based on my understanding, I see two possible interpretations:

1. 00:00:40 00:00:00
This format indicates 40 days and zero hours, minutes, and seconds.
2. 00:01:10 00:00:00
This format implies a difference of 1 month, 10 days, and zero hours, minutes, and seconds.

Could you please provide some guidance on how to correctly format a time difference of 40 days in the "years:months:days hours:minutes:seconds" format? Additionally, if there are any other examples of larger time differences, I would greatly appreciate knowing those.

Best regards,
Orvill

If in doubt I'd recommend running the function with different sets of values on some test data and check the results. The "undo" parameter may be helpful here.

messages.subject_clean: get psi and p from the MSOM run via communityModel
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
There are two options for obtaining species-level parameters.

1) add the parameters to the monitored parameters, e.g.
mod.jags@params <- c(mod.jags@params, "psi", "p")

This will return the estimates for psi and p for all species, stations (and occasions, for p) directly from the the model fitting process. The order of indices is [species, station, occasion]. Just be aware that including "p" can lead to very large outputs.

2) Use the predict() function. This only works for psi though, not p.
predict(
    object = mod.jags,
    mcmc.list = fit.jags,
    type = "psi",
    x = data_list$siteCovs)

Here we use the site covariates at the camera trap stations as input for the prediction (argument "x"). You can of course provide different data for the prediction.

Both 1 and 2 only work for species parameters though. The community values are not returned explicitly and would need to be calculated manually at the moment.

Best regards,
Jürgen
